question: Build a payout-definition bridge on the repository's corrected FY2020-24 sponsor panel: compute (a) grants / beginning assets, (b) the IRS/IPS formula grants / (year-end assets + grants), (c) sponsor medians with and without the >=$1m filter and processors, and (d) the same net of R5 DAF-to-DAF transfers. Reproduce IPS's 9.7% FY2023 median, then set the result beside the DAFRC 2024 account-level median (9%, 22% inactive) to show how much of the 23.9%-vs-9% gap is denominator, sponsor weighting or within-sponsor distribution
conclusion_affected: §1 payout bullets and the 'fund-level payout is not public' sentence; §11.1 net payout
rationale: The literature quotes 9.7% (IPS 2025, sponsor median, IRS formula), 9% (DAFRC 2024, account median), 3.1% (CMF 2021, Michigan CF accounts) and 23.9% (NPT, aggregate), and Leff 2025 treats the spread as unresolved. The repo has the panel to separate the definitional part (a, b, c) from the distributional part (account-level) in one table. The account-level part cannot be computed from public data and must cite DAFRC

question: Test the California AG audit finding that community foundations sent the highest share of DAF grants to other DAFs (18% vs 10% commercial) against the R5 netting rule: for California CFs in the AG sample universe (>$10m DAF assets) read TY2021-24 Schedule I lines to national sponsors and other CFs, and split them into grants to recipients' DAFs versus pooled or field-of-interest funds where the filing allows
conclusion_affected: R5 DAF-to-DAF netting central estimate; framing of sponsor-to-sponsor flows as mainly national-to-national (§1 payout bullet; §11.1)
rationale: CA AG (2022, 57 sponsors, 2016-2020) finds about 11% of grants went to other DAFs overall, matching the repo's 10-18%, but CFs were highest at 18%. The repo weights CF recipients by their DAF share of assets and reports 12.1% national-to-national. If CF outbound transfers are as large as the AG data suggest, R5 under-nets CF payout

question: From an environment where SSRN abstract pages load (or from author pages), review and add to the literature register: Essig Aberg 2024 'Tax Elasticities of Top Donors' (doi:10.2139/ssrn.4969635; check for a DAF-specific tax elasticity usable in an OBBBA 0.5%-floor scenario), Flannery & Mittendorf 2025 'When DAFs Draw the Map' (doi:10.2139/ssrn.5401950; local vs non-local DAF grants at CFs), Krueger 2026 (doi:10.2139/ssrn.6087686); also the full CMF 2021 Michigan report and Beebe 2024 (Baker Institute), both blocked here
conclusion_affected: Completeness of the 2021-26 literature review; possible DAF-specific tax-response evidence for §6 (OBBBA)
rationale: Crossref confirms these works exist, but SSRN returned a Cloudflare challenge, michiganfoundations.org/system/files is robots-disallowed and bakerinstitute.org returned 403, so none was reviewed. No DAF-specific tax-elasticity or bunching econometrics for 2021-26 was otherwise found; Essig Aberg is the only candidate
